bimodal_title: A theory of mouse and keyboard together
bimodal_p1: The extension exists to promote a UI theory we call Bimodal Control. Steer the cursor with the mouse as before, but activate with keyboard keys instead of mouse buttons. Hover a link and press $F$ to click it, or $G$ to open it in a new background tab. This is fast. It’s called a key-click.
bimodal_p2: A number of key actions are available besides $F$. That’s where the power emerges in KeyPilot: a keyboard layout with lots of key-click functions, customizable in the built-in Layout Config editor. It is free and under the MIT License.
bimodal_p3: The key-click animation on this page shows the gesture: point with the mouse, press $F$ to open, then $D$ to go back.
